deed: Recha Freier announced the founding of Youth Aliyah on the day Hitler came to power
title: Recha Freier founded Youth Aliyah on the day Hitler came to power, and the organization brought thousands of young people out of Germany

trailer.text: Recha Freier, a musician and social activist born in Germany, founded Youth Aliyah in 1933, according to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in 1932 her husband asked her to help five teenage boys who complained that they could not find work because they were Jews.
One night it occurred to her that the boys should go to Palestine and be trained there as agricultural pioneers.
According to the encyclopedia Women in World History, on January 30, 1933, the day Hitler was appointed chancellor of Germany, Freier announced the establishment of the Society for Youth Aliyah.
According to the same encyclopedia, Freier, an Israeli Zionist leader, rescued thousands of young Jews from Nazi Germany as the founder of Youth Aliyah.

glance.label: Scale
glance.value: Thousands of young people rescued from Nazi Germany

paragraphs.text: According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, Recha Schweitzer was born on October 29, 1892, to Orthodox parents.
As a child she encountered antisemitism in her hometown, in the form of a notice in the local park.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, she was a teacher and a scholar of folklore.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in 1919 Recha married Rabbi Dr. Moritz Freier, and they had three sons and a daughter.
According to Women in World History, in the early 1930s many German Jews who had once been prosperous were struggling or out of work.
The prospects of Jewish youth finding work were dim.
According to the same encyclopedia, in February 1932 16-year-old Nathan Höxter approached Freier.
He led five friends in a Zionist youth group in Berlin, and asked her to help them find work.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, it was her husband who asked her to help the five boys.
In 1952 Freier said, according to Jewish Currents, that young people she knew had lost their jobs and their whole future in Germany because they were Jews.
So, she said, she had the idea of taking them to the Land of Israel and training them for a future on the land.
She wrote that the utter senselessness of Jewish life in the Diaspora stood before her eyes.
According to Israeled, the idea was born in 1932, when Freier sent Henrietta Szold a letter with a plan to bring Jewish youth from Germany to Palestine.
Szold rejected the proposal.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, Jewish organizations and parents were skeptical about the plan to send children alone to a distant country.
According to Women in World History, many parents were extremely skeptical about sending their sons and daughters, aged 14–17, to a far-off desert land.
According to Kenyon College, part of the Jewish community in Germany regarded Freier's methods as illegal, and part opposed separating children from their parents.

According to Women in World History, while visiting Dr. Georg Landauer, head of the Eretz Israel Department of the Zionist Organization in Berlin, Freier happened to read a circular that was to be sent to the organization's branches, warning them against her "reckless" plan. She hid the entire printing in her handbag and threw it into a garbage pail on her way home.
She hid the entire printing in her handbag and threw it into a garbage pail on her way home.
According to Women in World History, on January 30, 1933, the day Adolf Hitler was appointed chancellor of Germany, Freier announced the official establishment of the Society for Youth Aliyah.
According to Jewish Currents, the organization was originally called the Committee for the Assistance of Jewish Youth, and it opened its office in Berlin on that day.
According to the Leo Baeck Institute, the committee later became known as Jugend-Aliyah.
According to Israeled, Szold continued to refuse to provide immigration certificates, so Freier set up her own organization in order to lobby the Mandatory government directly.
According to the Jewish Museum Berlin, for Freier the founding on the day Hitler came to power was a logical consequence of her long Zionist commitment to promoting immigration to Palestine.
According to the museum, the idea was to train the young people not in Germany but in the settlements in Palestine.
Entry certificates were easier to obtain for students aged 14 to 17, and this served the approach of Youth Aliyah.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, the committee provided the organization and support for carrying out Youth Aliyah from Germany.
According to Israeled, Freier raised funds and began sending the first youths in October 1932.
According to Women in World History, Nathan Höxter and his group arrived in Jaffa on December 2, 1932.
According to the Jewish Museum Berlin, in May 1933 the organization signed detailed housing and training contracts for the first group with Kibbutz Ein Harod.
That same month Freier traveled to Palestine to win over to her plan Henrietta Szold, whom the encyclopedia Women in World History calls the most powerful woman in the Zionist movement.
According to the same encyclopedia, on November 27, 1933, Szold became director of the Youth Aliyah organization in Palestine, which was still largely theoretical.
According to Women in World History, on February 19, 1934, the first organized group of young emigrants from Germany arrived in Haifa harbor on board the ship Martha Washington.
According to Kenyon College, Ben Shemen took in approximately 100 Youth Aliyah children in 1934.
According to Women in World History, in the first two years 363 immigrants reached Palestine in 1934 and 550 in 1935, a relatively modest number.

According to the author of the entry in the encyclopedia Women in World History, Youth Aliyah, which brought a total of 30,353 young people to Palestine between 1934 and 1948, should be considered "by any criterion" the most successful rescue project of young Jews during the entire Holocaust period.
The sources give different numbers for the children rescued; they are listed here alongside.

According to Jewish Currents, the organization was involved in bringing some 300,000 young people to Israel from North Africa, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, the Soviet Union and Ethiopia.
According to Women in World History, at the World Zionist Congress in Lucerne in 1935 Szold publicly acknowledged Freier as leader of the Youth Aliyah movement.
According to Israeled, only toward the end of her life did Freier receive recognition as the founder of Youth Aliyah.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in 1975, at the age of eighty-three, she received an honorary doctorate from the Hebrew University.
In 1981 she received the Israel Prize for her special merits.
According to Jewish Currents, the Youth Aliyah organization itself had already received the Israel Prize in 1958.
According to Israeled, Freier died on April 2, 1984, in Jerusalem.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in November 1984 the City Council of Berlin-Charlottenburg affixed a commemorative plaque at the Jewish Community Center in Fasanen Street.

According to Women in World History, in April 1990 the West German ambassador to Israel and the mayor of East Berlin attended the cornerstone laying for the Recha Freier Educational Center at Kibbutz Yakum.
According to Kenyon College, an Israeli postage stamp was issued in her honor in 2018.
Freier did not leave music behind.
According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, in 1958 she founded the Israel Composers' Fund to foster original musical composition.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in 1966 she founded the "Testimonium" together with the composer Roman Haubenstock-Ramati.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, after September 1939 Freier succeeded, by illegal means, in getting Polish Jews out of concentration camps and helping them go on to Palestine.
Following the conflict over this action, she was suspended from all her functions in Youth Aliyah.
According to IFCJ, she stole 100 permits issued by the Nazis and used them to free camp prisoners, and because of this she was pushed out of the leadership of the Zionist movement in Berlin.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in 1940, after the Palestine Office of Youth Aliyah removed her, Freier had to leave Nazi Germany.

According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, after Freier sent a telegram to Berlin threatening a worldwide scandal, smugglers brought a first group of children from Germany to Zagreb, and in the following weeks one hundred and twenty children and teenagers arrived in Yugoslavia.
Freier said, according to the same encyclopedia, that she sent a telegram from Yugoslavia to Berlin threatening a world-wide scandal if the children did not come.
According to the same encyclopedia, she and her daughter went on to Syria and arrived in Palestine in March 1941.

According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, Szold told Freier that there was no position open for her anywhere in the organization in Palestine, and the differences between them prevented her from continuing her work.
According to Women in World History, a 1944 Jewish Agency exhibition marking a decade of Youth Aliyah made no mention of Freier's rescue efforts in the heart of Nazi Germany.
According to the same encyclopedia, during the difficult years in Palestine Freier was often depressed, and at times suicidal.
According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, Szold was frequently, and incorrectly, assumed to be the founder of Youth Aliyah.
In most accounts of the Holocaust Freier has been underestimated or not mentioned at all.

According to the Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, in her later years Freier occasionally felt bitter that her work for Youth Aliyah did not receive proper recognition and that Szold was mistakenly considered its founder.

disagreements.question: In what year was Youth Aliyah founded?

Encyclopedia of Jewish Women, at one point in the entry: in Berlin in 1932

disagreements.question: Who founded the Jewish Youth Aid?

versions.says: Jewish Museum Berlin: Adam Simonson founded it on January 30, 1933, together with six other activists
Jewish Museum Berlin: Recha Freier is the founder

disagreements.question: When did the first youths leave or arrive?

versions.says: Israeled: Freier began sending the first youths in October 1932
Women in World History: Höxter and his group arrived in Jaffa on December 2, 1932
Jewish Museum Berlin: the young people left Europe in February 1934, and by then their number had dropped from a planned 60 to 43

disagreements.question: How many children did the organization rescue?

versions.says: Women in World History: 5,012 young people immigrated by September 1939
Women in World History: 30,353 young people between 1934 and 1948
Jewish Currents: Freier saved at least 7,000 Jewish and Austrian children before the war
Israeled: more than 11,000 children during World War II
Kenyon College: Freier helped more than 5,000 children escape from Germany
Michael Bulmash, in the Kenyon College collection: 30,000 children from Nazi Europe
Jewish Museum Berlin: more than twenty-one thousand young people from Germany

disagreements.question: How many children left Yugoslavia with Freier or with her help?

versions.says: Encyclopedia of Jewish Women: eighty traveled to Palestine and forty reached Switzerland
Women in World History: Freier secured passage for herself, her daughter and 90 of her children
Kenyon College: a group of 40 teenagers joined her when she settled in Palestine in 1941
Jewish Currents: she arranged transit for eighty young people in Yugoslavia
Encyclopedia of Jewish Women: in Norden, East Friesland
Encyclopaedia Judaica: in "Nordeney", Germany

disagreements.question: What was her husband's first name?

IFCJ: she married Rabbi Moshe Freier, and they raised three sons in Germany

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, רחה פריאר, פעילה חברתית ומוזיקאית שנולדה בגרמניה, ייסדה את עליית הנוער ב-1933, בדיוק כשהיטלר עלה לשלטון.
claims.quote: A social activist and musician, German-born Recha Freier founded Youth Aliyah in 1933, just as Hitler came to power.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, ב-1932 בעלה של פריאר ביקש ממנה לעזור לחמישה נערים שלא מצאו עבודה כי היו יהודים.
claims.quote: That year her husband had asked her to help five teenage boys who complained that they could not find any work because they were Jews.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, באחד הלילות עלה בדעתה של פריאר הרעיון שהנערים ייסעו לפלשתינה ויוכשרו בהתיישבויות עובדים כחלוצים חקלאיים.
claims.quote: One night an idea came to her: the boys should go to Palestine to be trained in workers’ settlements as agricultural pioneers.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, ב-30 בינואר 1933, היום שבו מונה אדולף היטלר לקנצלר גרמניה, הכריזה רחה פריאר על הקמתה הרשמית של האגודה לעליית הנוער.
claims.quote: On January 30, 1933, the day that Adolf Hitler was appointed chancellor of Germany, Freier announced the official establishment of the Society for Youth Aliyah.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, פריאר הייתה מנהיגה ציונית ישראלית שנולדה בגרמניה והצילה אלפי יהודים צעירים מגרמניה הנאצית כמייסדת עליית הנוער.
claims.quote: German-born Israeli Zionist leader, teacher, and writer who, as the founder of Youth Aliyah, rescued thousands of young Jews from Nazi Germany.

claims.quote: Immediately after the Nazis seized power, on January 30, 1933, Berlin-based Recha Freier founded the Jüdische Jugendhilfe

claims.quote: Having been responsible for the emigration to Palestine of a total of 30,353 from 1934 to 1948, by any criterion Youth Aliyah must be recognized as the most successful rescue project of young Jews during the entire Holocaust period.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, עד פרוץ מלחמת העולם השנייה בספטמבר 1939 עלו לפלשתינה 5,012 בני נוער.
claims.quote: By the outbreak of World War II in September 1939, 5,012 had been able to immigrate to Palestine

claims.text: לפי Jewish Currents, לפני פרוץ המלחמה ב-1939 פריאר הייתה אחראית להצלת לפחות 7,000 ילדים יהודים ואוסטרים באמצעות העברתם.
claims.quote: Before the war broke out in 1939, Freier was responsible for saving at least 7,000 Jewish and Austrian children by arranging their transport, both legal and illegal

claims.text: לפי Israeled, התוכנית, שנקראה אחר כך עליית הנוער, הצילה יותר מ-11,000 ילדים יהודים במהלך מלחמת העולם השנייה.
claims.quote: rescues more than 11,000 Jewish children during World War II

claims.text: לפי מכללת קניון, פריאר סייעה ליותר מ-5,000 ילדים יהודים להימלט מגרמניה.
claims.quote: she helped more than 5,000 Jewish children escape from Germany.

claims.text: לפי מידע שמסר מייקל בולמש באוסף של מכללת קניון, עליית הנוער שייסדה פריאר הצילה 30,000 ילדים יהודים מאירופה הנאצית.
claims.quote: the organization founded by Recha Freier responsible for rescuing 30,000 Jewish children from Nazi Europe.

claims.text: לפי המוזיאון היהודי בברלין, הארגון הציל יותר מעשרים ואחד אלף צעירים יהודים מגרמניה.
claims.quote: marked the start of the rescue of more than twenty-one thousand young German Jews by the organization.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Currents, הארגון היה מעורב בהבאת כ-300,000 צעירים לישראל מצפון אפריקה, אירופה, אמריקה הלטינית, ברית המועצות ואתיופיה.
claims.quote: The organization has been involved in bringing some 300,000 young people to Israel from North Africa, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, the USSR, and Ethiopia.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, בקונגרס הציוני העולמי בלוצרן ב-1935 הכירה סולד בפומבי בפריאר כמנהיגת תנועת עליית הנוער.
claims.quote: World Zionist Congress held in Lucerne, Switzerland, in 1935 when Szold publicly acknowledged her as leader of the Youth Aliyah movement.

claims.text: לפי Israeled, רק לקראת סוף חייה זכתה פריאר להכרה כמייסדת עליית הנוער, ב-1981 הוענק לה פרס ישראל והיא מתה ב-2 באפריל 1984 בירושלים.
claims.quote: Only toward the end of her life does Freier receive recognition as the founder of Youth Aliyah. In 1981 she is awarded the Israel Prize. She dies April 2, 1984, in Jerusalem.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, בנובמבר 1984 הצמידה מועצת העיר ברלין-שרלוטנבורג לוח זיכרון במרכז הקהילה היהודית ברחוב פזאנן לכבוד מייסדת עליית הנוער.
claims.quote: In November of that year the City Council of Berlin-Charlottenburg affixed a commemorative plaque at the Jewish Community Center in Fasanen Street

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, באפריל 1990 נכחו שגריר מערב גרמניה בישראל וראש עיריית מזרח ברלין בטקס הנחת אבן הפינה למרכז החינוכי על שם רחה פריאר בקיבוץ יקום.
claims.quote: In April 1990, the West German ambassador to Israel and the mayor of what was then still East Berlin attended the cornerstone laying ceremony for the Recha Freier Educational Center at Kibbutz Yakum near Herzliya.

claims.text: לפי מכללת קניון, בולו דואר ישראלי הונפק לכבודה של פריאר ב-2018.
claims.quote: An Israeli postage stamp was issued in her honor in 2018.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, ב-1958 ייסדה פריאר את קרן המלחינים הישראלית לעידוד יצירה מוזיקלית מקורית.
claims.quote: She founded the Israel Composers' Fund in 1958 to foster original musical compositions

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, ב-1966 ייסדה פריאר את "טסטימוניום" יחד עם המלחין רומן האובנשטוק-רמאטי.
claims.quote: In 1966 she founded the Testimonium, together with the avant-garde composer Roman Haubenstock-Ramati

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, לאחר ספטמבר 1939 פריאר הצליחה, באמצעים בלתי חוקיים, להוציא יהודים פולנים ממחנות ריכוז ולסייע להם להמשיך לפלשתינה.
claims.quote: Unafraid of using illegal means to help the Polish men, she succeeded in getting some of them out of the concentration camps, helping them to go on to Palestine.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, בעקבות הסכסוך סביב פעולתה זו הושעתה פריאר מכל תפקידיה בעליית הנוער.
claims.quote: Eventually she was suspended from all her functions in the Youth Aliyah.

claims.text: לפי IFCJ, פריאר גנבה 100 אישורים שהנפיקו הנאצים והשתמשה בהם כדי לשחרר אסירי מחנות ולשלחם לארץ, ובגלל זה נדחקה מהנהגת התנועה הציונית בברלין.
claims.quote: At one point, Recha swiped 100 permits issued by the Nazis and used them to free camp prisoners awaiting death, sending them to the Holy Land.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, ב-1940, אחרי שמשרד ארץ ישראל של עליית הנוער הרחיק אותה, נאלצה פריאר לעזוב את גרמניה הנאצית.
claims.quote: After she was banned by the Palestine office of Youth Aliyah in 1940, Recha Freier had to leave Nazi Germany.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, בשבועות שלאחר מכן הגיעו ליוגוסלביה מאה ועשרים ילדים ובני נוער מגרמניה.
claims.quote: In the next few weeks one hundred and twenty children and teenagers arrived.

claims.text: פריאר סיפרה, לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, ששלחה מיוגוסלביה מברק לברלין ואיימה בשערורייה עולמית אם הילדים לא יגיעו.
claims.quote: Hundreds of immigration certificates lay here and if the children do not come, I will make a world-wide scandal of the situation.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, פריאר וביתה המשיכו לסוריה והגיעו לפלשתינה במרץ 1941.
claims.quote: They then proceeded to Syria and arrived in Palestine in March 1941.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, סולד אמרה לפריאר שאין לה תפקיד פנוי בשום מקום בארגון בפלשתינה, וההבדלים ביניהן מנעו ממנה להמשיך בעבודתה בעליית הנוער.
claims.quote: Szold told her that there was no position open for her anywhere within the organization in Palestine.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, בתערוכה של הסוכנות היהודית ב-1944, שצוינה בה עשור של עליית הנוער, לא הוזכרו מאמצי ההצלה של פריאר בלב גרמניה הנאצית.
claims.quote: a Jewish Agency exhibition in 1944 in which a decade of Youth Aliyah work was commemorated without a single mention of her rescue efforts in the heart of Nazi Germany.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, בשנים הקשות בפלשתינה פריאר סבלה לעיתים קרובות מדיכאון ולעיתים מנטיות אובדניות.
claims.quote: During these difficult years, she was often depressed and at times suicidal.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, סולד הוחזקה לעתים קרובות, בטעות, למייסדת עליית הנוער.
claims.quote: As a result, she was frequently (and incorrectly) assumed to be the founder of the Youth Aliyah.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, ברוב תיאורי השואה פריאר זכתה להערכת חסר או לא הוזכרה כלל.
claims.quote: However, in most accounts of the Holocaust she has either been underestimated or totally unacknowledged.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, בשנותיה המאוחרות פריאר חשה מרירות על כך שעבודתה בעליית הנוער לא זכתה להכרה ראויה ושסולד נחשבה בטעות למייסדת.
claims.quote: In her later years Freier occasionally felt bitter that her earlier work for the Youth Aliyah was never properly recognized and that Henrietta Szold was mistakenly considered its founder.

claims.text: הערך באנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות מציין בנקודה אחת שפריאר ייסדה את עליית הנוער בברלין ב-1932.
claims.quote: By founding the Youth Aliyah (Jugend-Alijah) in Berlin, Germany in 1932, Recha Freier saved thousands of Jewish lives.

claims.text: לפי מוזיאון היהודי בברלין, ב-30 בינואר 1933 אדם סימונסון ייסד את הסיוע לנוער יהודי יחד עם שישה פעילים נוספים.
claims.quote: On 30 January 1933 Adam Simonson founded the Jewish Youth Aid together with six other activists.

claims.text: לפי המוזיאון היהודי בברלין, הצעירים עזבו את אירופה בפברואר 1934, ועד אז מספר העולים המתוכנן, שישים, צנח לארבעים ושלושה.
claims.quote: The young people left Europe in February 1934. By that time the originally planned number of sixty emigrants had dwindled to forty-three.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, אחרי שהגיעו שמונים אישורי עלייה נסעו שמונים ילדים לפלשתינה, וארבעים הנותרים הגיעו בסופו של דבר לשווייץ.
claims.quote: After eighty certificates arrived, eighty children traveled to Palestine. The remaining forty eventually reached Switzerland, where they remained till the end of the war.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיה Women in World History, עד התקפת גרמניה על יוגוסלביה באפריל 1941 הצליחה פריאר להבטיח מעבר לעצמה, לבתה ול-90 מילדיה.
claims.quote: she had been able to secure passage for herself, her daughter, and 90 of her brood.

claims.text: לפי מכללת קניון, פריאר התיישבה לצמיתות בפלשתינה ב-1941 וקבוצה של 40 בני נוער הצטרפה אליה.
claims.quote: Freier herself would eventually take up permanent residence in Palestine in 1941, taking a group of 40 teenagers with her.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Currents, פריאר עזבה את גרמניה רק ב-1940, ובדרכה לפלשתינה ארגנה מעבר לשמונים צעירים ביוגוסלביה.
claims.quote: She did not leave Germany until 1940; en route to Palestine, she arranged transit for eighty young people in Yugoslavia.

claims.text: לפי אנציקלופדיית הנשים היהודיות, ב-1919 נישאה רחה לרב ד"ר מוריץ פריאר, ונולדו להם שלושה בנים ובת.
claims.quote: In 1929 the couple welcomed a daughter, Ma’ayan.
